passages.title: L-A
passages.text: In the UK, nursery and primary education are for younger children, secondary school covers the teenage years, sixth form colleges help students prepare for university, further education colleges often provide vocational courses, universities offer degree programmes, and adult education allows learners to study later in life.

audios.title: Education options: tutor and student
audios.transcript:
Tutor: Today we are comparing places to study in the UK. A nursery school is for very young children, while primary school follows as children grow. Secondary school covers the teenage years.
Student: What if a sixteen-year-old wants to prepare for university?
Tutor: A sixth form college is one option. A further education college is different: it often offers vocational courses. That is the college in our first conversation. A university offers degree programmes. Information A on your worksheet refers to a university.
Student: Can adults return to study?
Tutor: Yes. Adult education lets people study later in life. And parents of younger children can choose a nursery school.
